title: PrettyConfig
description: This is mainly to generate a pretty and accurate config JSON SCHEMA

backend.description: Which backend to use, see backends.rs

check_contrast.description: This flags ensures good contrast between images, by doing some w3m calculations. However it isn't required and should only be turn on when you notice bad contrast between many images.

color_space.description: Which colorspace to use, see colorspaces.rs

env_vars.description: Enables the use of enviromental variables in the targets template paths

fallback_generator.description: How to 'generate' colors when there aren't enough colors to create the `palette`. This appears as "Artificially generating colors.." in cli

palette.description: Which palette to use, see palettes.rs

saturation.description: Maybe the user requires more vivid colors

templates.description: The [templates] header, here you can define multiple templates

threshold.description: What threshold to use to differentiate colors, if not defined, wallust automatically looks for the best fit

Backend.description: This indicates what 'parser' method to use, defined in the config file. Corresponds to the modules inside this module

oneOf.description: Read and return the whole image pixels (more precision, slower)
Resizes the image before parsing, mantaining it's aspect ratio
Uses image magick `convert` to generate the colors, like pywal
Faster algo hardcoded to 512x512 (no ratio respected)
A much faster resize algo that uses SIMD. For some reason it fails on some images where `resized` doesn't, for this reason it doesn't *replace* but rather it's a new option.
Kmeans is an algo that divides and picks pixels all around the image, giving a more diverse look.

ColorSpace.description: Corresponds to the modules inside this module and `color_space` parameter in the config file.

oneOf.description: Uses Cie L*a*b color space
Variant of `lab` that mixes the colors gathered, if not enough colors it fallbacks to usual lab (not recommended in small images)
CIE Lch, you can understand this color space like LAB but with chrome and hue added. Could help when sorting.
CIE Lch, you can understand this color space like LAB but with chrome and hue added. Could help when sorting.
Variant of Lch which preserves 8 colors: black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan and gray. This works best with 'darkansi' palette, allowing a constant color order.
uses [`interpolate`]
uses [`complementary`]

Fields.description: An entry within the config file, toml table ref: <https://toml.io/en/v1.0.0#array-of-tables>

pywal.description: Allows pywal template spec compatibility (disabled by default)

template.description: A file inside `~/.config/wallust/`, which is used for templating

Palette.description: Corresponds to the modules inside this module and `palette` parameter in the config file.

oneOf.description: 8 dark colors, dark background and light contrast
Same as `dark` but uses the 16 colors trick
This is a `dark` variant that changes all colors to it's complementary counterpart, giving the feeling of a 'new palette' but that still makes sense with the image provided.
16 variation of the dark complementary variant

This is not a 'dark' variant, is a new palette that is meant to work with `lchansi` colorspace, which will maintain 'tty' like color order and only adjusting the colors acording to the theme. A possible solution for LS_COLORS and the like. Should workout with other colorspace, but the result may not be optimal.
The ansidark palette with 16 color variation.
Same as `dark` with hard hue colors
Harddark with 16 color variation
complementary colors variation of harddark scheme
complementary colors variation of harddark scheme
Light bg, dark fg
Same as `light` but uses the 16 color trick
complementary colors variation of light
complementary colors variation of light with the 16 color variation
Variant of softlight, uses the lightest colors and a dark background (could be interpreted as `dark` inversed)
softdark with 16 color variation
complementary variation for softdark
complementary variation for softdark with the 16 color variation
Light with soft pastel colors, counterpart of `harddark`
softlight with 16 color variation
softlight with complementary colors
softlight with complementary colors with 16 colors
